items.title: Randy Weston — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: We organized this festival and I brought over ... Pucho and His Latin Soul Brothers ... We had this three-day festival at a bullring in Tangiers.

ctx.x: Yeah. So to get there you have to take donkeys, but the guys in the band didn’t know this. So when we got to the staging place where you start to go up the mountain, here you got Al Hayward, you got all the guys, you know? Billy Harper was the only one that was cool, because Billy, being from Texas, he knew how to ride horses and donkeys. Anyhow, seeing these guys with their musical instruments…Tom McKenzie was the bass player. Seeing these guys going up the mountains on these donkeys, with their instruments,…

Mandrill, and Pucho and His Latin Soul Brothers, and we had 40 African musicians. We had this three-day festival at a bullring in Tangiers. Two nights it was at the bullring and the next night it was a Sahara sandstorm coming from the Sahara. We couldn’t play in the bull right so we had to rush and clean up this theatre called Theatre Cervantes in Tangiers. That was an experience, and I having that club, that was an experience. We had a blues band from Chicago sometime. We had singers from the Congo…we played…
